hardBlockers.description: FAIL when harness validation shows that the stage did not leave the required committed repository state.
FAIL when the implementation contradicts a recorded acceptance criterion or confirmed Product Owner decision.
FAIL when the change introduces a tool, dependency, or pattern prohibited by project instructions.
FAIL when tests pass independently of the behavior they claim to verify or required checks were weakened.
FAIL when required implementation is uncommitted, the worktree is dirty, or a required check is failing.

requirements.description: Implement every recorded acceptance criterion without unrelated scope.
Add tests that directly prove the required success, rejection, and failure behavior.
Complete required persistence, migration, queue, worker, HTTP, and application wiring.
Record one direct observation of the delivered behavior running, beyond a passing test suite.
Write onto the task record what changed, what was observed and how, what was not verified, and anything left unwired or deferred.

dimensions.description: How completely and accurately the implementation realizes the recorded acceptance behavior.
dimensions.good: B requires all specified behavior to work with no known material defect.
dimensions.excellent: A requires complete behavior with robust handling of the recorded edge and failure cases.

dimensions.description: How the work advances: test first, small verified steps, each commit a safe unit of progress.
dimensions.good: B requires small coherent commits whose tests cover the behavior they introduce.
dimensions.excellent: A requires a commit sequence where each step is independently revertable and the tests visibly drove the design.

dimensions.description: How well the implementation fits project structure while keeping responsibilities and dependencies clear.
dimensions.good: B requires idiomatic, focused code with no unnecessary coupling or complexity.
dimensions.excellent: A requires a minimal design that narrows future defect space and is straightforward to change.

dimensions.description: How directly and reliably the tests detect regressions in required behavior.
dimensions.good: B requires behavior-focused tests whose failures depend on the implemented behavior.
dimensions.excellent: A requires strong boundary and failure coverage without brittle implementation coupling.

dimensions.description: How consistently the change follows the repository's stack, conventions, and operational model.
dimensions.good: B requires full compliance with established patterns or explicitly justified deviations.
dimensions.excellent: A requires seamless integration that reuses stable project mechanisms without incidental complexity.
